Suo-Moto-Rule No. 420 of 1998
With
Civil Revision No. 4722 of 1997
lawyer:
Mr. J.N. Deb, Advocate ----- For petitioners 
Mr. Suvash Chandra Saha, Advocate ----- For opposite parties
parties:
Mr. Abdul Jalil and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.

full_judgment:
Mr. Bijan Kumar Das, J. This Suo-Moto Rule was issued calling upon the heirs of the deceased opposite party No.12 Md. Mamtaz Ali Khan to show cause as to why the application for making the rule absolute with finding that the impugned judgment and decree being passed in favour of a dead person is a nullity should not be allowed or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. The present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.269 of 1975 in the First Court of the then Munsif, Sylhet impleding several persons as defendants including Md. Mamtaz All Khan, who was, defendant No.12 in the suit wherein a prayer for declaration that the ex-parte decree dated 02.08.1974 passed in Title Suit No.146 of 1971 of the Sadar Munsif, First Court, Sylhet is collusive, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs. On transfer to the Additional Munsif Court, the said suit was re-numbered as Title Suit No.131 of 1973. 

 5. The trial Court by judgment and decree dated 17.11.1983 decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs declaring that the decree dated 02.08.1974 passed in Title Suit No.131 of 1970 of Additional Munsif Court, Sylhet is null and void, not binding upon the plaintiffs and it dose not cast any cloud over title of the plaintiffs in respect of their purchased properties which were subject matter of the suit. 

 6. The defendant No.12 alone as appellant then preferred Title Appeal No.1 1 of 1984 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet. The appeal was heard by the Additional District Judge, Sylhet who by judgment and decree dated 31.08.1997 allowed the appeal, reversed the judgment and decree of the trail Court and dismissed the plaintiff's suit being Title Suit No.269 of 1975. 

 7. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree, the plaintiffs initially obtained a rule being Civil Revision No.4722 of 1997. Subsequently in connection with the said rule the aforesaid connected Suo-moto rule was issued on the application filed by the petitioners stating that during pendency of the appeal before the lower appellate court the sole appellant Md. Mamtaz Ali Khan died on 17.11.1991 leaving behind his heirs as disclosed in paragraph No.4 of the application. It is also stated that the said Mamtaz Ali Khan was the sole appellant and application for substitution of his heirs was filed before the appellate court on 17.02.1992 after 90 days of the date of death of the sole appellant and no order was passed on the said application which remained unattended all through. It is accordingly stated that the lower appellate court when passed the judgment and decree had no jurisdiction to pass the decree in favour' of a dead person and therefore the judgment and decree dated 31.08.1997 passed by the lower appellate court in Title Appeal No.11 of 1984 is a nullity. The decree of the lower appellate court contained the name of the aforesaid Md. Mamtaz Ali Khan and accordingly the petitioners' obtained the rule by impledading Md. Mamtaz Khan as opposite party No.12 in Civil Revision No.4722 of 1997 and subsequently having learnt about the death of the deceased sole appellant collected the names of the heirs and filed the application upon which a learned Single Judge of this Division issue the aforesaid Suo-Moto Rule against the heirs of the deceased opposite party No.12 Md. Mamtaz Ali Khan. In view of the order of this Bench dated 27.07.2004, the office made a note on 01.08.2004 stating that the rule is not ready for hearing as all the exhibits filed before the trial court were not available with the lower court records. This matter appeared in the list on 02.08.2004 as fixed earlier and the matter was taken up on 03.08.2004 as both the learned Advocates submitted that the records would not be necessary for disposal of the rule. 

 8. Mr. J.N. Deb, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the lower appellate court committed a gross error of law in passing a decree in favour of the sole deceased appellant who had no jurisdiction to pass such decree and accordingly the judgment and decree of the lower appellate court is a nullity. In support of his submission, Mr. Deb has relied on a decision in the case of Jiviben Lavji Raganath vs. Jadavji Devshanker and others reported in AIR 1978, Gujrat 32. Mr. Deb also submits that an application for substitution of the heirs of the deceased sole appellant was filled before the lower appellate court which was beyond 90 days from the date of the death of the deceased sole appellant and no prayer for setting aside abatement was made and that the said application for substitution was not moved or pressed and no order was passed on that application. According to Mr. Deb, the appeal stood abated for non-substitution of the heirs of the deceased sole appellant and on that score also the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court was nullity. In support of submission Mr. Deb has relied on a decision in the case of Bhupati Biswas and others Vs. Niranjan Biswas and others reported in 40 DLR 517. 

 10. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for both the parties and perused the materials available before the court. There is no dispute that Md. Mamtaz Ali khan, who was defendant No.12 in the suit, alone preferred Title Appeal No.11 of 1984 against the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in the suit. It is also not denied that the said sole appellant Md. Mamtaz Ali Khan died on 17.11.1991 during pendency of the appeal. Annexure "X" to the application upon which Suo-Moto rule was issued indicates that an application for substitution of the heirs of the deceased sole appellant Md. Mamtaz Ali Khan was field on 17.02.1992 but no order was passed on the said application. It therefore appears that the sole appellant Md. Mamtaz Ali died during pendency of the appeal and his heirs were not substituted during the pendency of the appeal and his heirs were not brought on record by way of substitution within 90 days from the date of the death of the said appellant, the appeal became non-existent and the appellate court had no inherent jurisdiction to pass any order and if a decree is passed in ignorance of the death of the deceased sole appellant, the decree passed in such appeal would be a nullity even if the decree is passed in favour of the deceased sole appellant. It further appears that in such a situation the appeal stood abated for non-substitution of the heirs of the deceased sole appellant within 90 days from the date of the death of the sole appellant and the appellate court in such facts becomes powerless to pass any order in the appeal. That the judgment passed against the sole deceased appellant is a nullity gets support from the decision cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioners as reported in AIR 1978 Gujrat 32. In the said decision a Division Bench has held that a decree passed in ignorance of the death of sole appellant is nullity. 

 11. Admittedly, the application for substitution was field on 17.02.1992 after about 93 days from the date of death the sole appellant on 17.11.1991. No order was passed on the said application. The said application was not moved or pressed. Since abatement of the appeal took place on the expiry of 90 days from the date of death of the sole appellant, the lower appellate court had no jurisdiction to pass the decree without setting aside abatement of the appeal which could be made only upon fulfilling the terms and conditions as laid down in Order 22 Rule 9(2) and (3) of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the present case, there was even no application for substitution of the heirs of the deceased sole appellant after setting aside abatement and there was no occasion for the lower appellate court to pass any order under Order 22 Rule 9(2) and (3) of the Code of Civil Procedure. Since abatement of the appeal had taken place the impugned judgment and decree dated 31.08.1997 passed by the learned Additional District Judge in Title Appeal No.11 of 1984 was a nullity. I therefore find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners. 

 13. In the result, this Suo-Moto Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 31.08.1997 passed by the Additional District Judge and Anti Smuggling Tribunal, Sylhet in Title Appeal No.11 of 1984 are hereby set aside and those of the trial court is restored. Consequently the connected Civil Revision No.4722 of 1997 stands discharged as the rule was obtained against a dead man.
